purpose: Determine whether the dominant q_H operator error identified by BC2-B3 is primarily caused by using one global 90..H layer-average state instead of hydraulic information localized near the water table.

reference.source: qualified BC2-A2 accepted pressure-head profiles and interval bottom exchange

ANCHOR_90_POINT.role: full moving-thickness secant using localized pressure head rather than averaged theta

pressure_head_sampling.method: piecewise-linear interpolation between accepted A2 pressure-head node values in depth
pressure_head_sampling.endpoint_zero: H is defined by the same strict linear negative-to-positive zero crossing
pressure_head_sampling.reason: This is an information-localization diagnostic, not a proposed production reconstruction.

time_alignment.primary: trapezoidal average of candidate q at accepted interval start and end states compared with interval-average Reference qH

metrics: implied required pressure head h_req(d)=d*(qH_ref/Ks-1) compared with sampled h(H-d)

adjudication.local_information_support_rule: Near-water-table information is supported when at least one frozen local-point diagnostic has both lower RMS and lower mean-absolute qH error than MOVING_LAYER_AVERAGE in both WATER_TABLE_RISING and WATER_TABLE_FALLING strata.
adjudication.consistent_distance_rule: A frozen distance is called consistently best only if it is component-wise minimum or tied minimum for both RMS and mean-absolute error in both moving direction strata; otherwise no preferred distance is declared.
